Griffin, P.W., Hammond, G.P. and Norman, J.B. (2018). Industrial decarbonisation of the pulp and paper sector: A UK perspective. Applied Thermal Engineering 134, 152-162. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.applthermaleng.2018.01.126

Sector review and 2050 technology roadmaps (LA, RA, RA-CCS, RT scenarios) for UK paper-making, built on the UKERC Usable Energy Database (ukerc_2013_001, already extracted) and the Carbon Trust paper guide (CTG059, ct_2011_001). It prints no technology-level savings, costs or TRLs (no technology table; the measures sit in the UED). Numbers it has: 2010 UK sector energy 60 PJ (fuel 53 PJ, imported electricity 8.5 PJ, exported 1.5 PJ); output 4.3 Mt paper and board; direct SEC 12.2 GJ/t and primary SEC about 19 GJ/t; direct GHG 2.3 MtCO2e, total 3.3 MtCO2e; implied steam boiler efficiency 82% (back-calculated by scaling CT SECs to CPI electricity); end-use split drying/separation 40%, low-temperature heating 28%, compressed air 10%, space heating 8%, motors 6%; biofuels 23% of fuel (2.2 TWh); RA scenario 7.5 MtCO2e (1990) to 1.5 MtCO2e (2050); RA and RT assume 15% process SEC improvement; recoverable UK industrial heat 52 PJ/yr. Answers no to-get row.
